segments.text: France locked in 295,000 tons of diesel a month, just over 10% of consumption. This is Omni
View Top World News, Episode 28. I'm Mira, the Nerra Network's AI host. After that fuel
deal, India's biggest share sale opens, a British banking app goes dark, Hanoi orders new
metro trains, and Seoul pulls more diplomats out of Ukraine. France 24 says the Elysée
split the new diesel into about 100,000 tons a month, from the Emirates and the same amount
from Bahrain. Still to be locked in later today. Saudi barrels sit on top of that total.
President Emanuel Macron is in the Emirates, Bahrain, and Qatar, chasing oil and diesel after
a weekend of violent protests over living costs. Those three states have been in turmoil since
February because of the U.S. Iran War. Crude has ballooned across eight months while Iran blockades
the Strait of Hormuz, the main way Gulf energy gets out. The G7, with France and the chair this year,
agreed early this month to draw as much as 100 million barrels from strategic reserves.
The presidency says Kuwait gave very clear commitments to send diesel and kerosene to
Mayotte and Reunion, routed through Oman so the ships avoid her mues.
Talks are also on to cut maritime insurance prices, so more cargo can use the straight
more cheaply.
Paris calls the Gulf Pledge's long-term energy security.
Mukesh Ambani, India's second richest man, is opening what the Guardian says could be
the country's largest-ever share sale, even with the market down.
Geo platforms backed by Meta and Google once to raise as much as 302 billion rupees, 2.4
billion pounds, from Wednesday.
The target valuation is 10.3 trillion rupees, 81 billion pounds in the Guardian's headline
figure.
The company is a decade-old, reliant subsidiary, run by Akash Ambani, and it sells low-cost
broadband to millions.
212 anchor investors signed on Monday, among them BlackRock, Singapore Sovereign Wealth Fund,
the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Fidelity, Shroters, JP Morgan Asset Management, Franklin
Templeton, Invesco and Prudential. Retail buyers get shares on Wednesday, and the offer
is due to close Friday. Reliance is filing last week set a range of 1,065 to 1,119 rupees
a share for up to 270 million new shares. More than 400,000 employees are being offered
a discount of 54 rupees a share. At the top of the range, Geo would rank 4th in India,
behind Reliance, Barti Airtel and HDFC Bank, and more than double the 4.9 trillion rupee
mark from Metta in Google's 2020 investment. That is still far under summer talk of more
than 110 billion pounds. The nifty 50 is down more than 12 percent this year. Reliance
Someone says Geo launched in September 2016, added 16 million subscribers in a month,
and passed 100 million in 170 days by starting a price war that made mobile internet cheaper.
It now says it will push into artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and digital infrastructure.
Director Isha Ambani told investors the idea began around 2009 or 10, when she and
Akash could not get a college assignment submitted because the connection failed.
Revolute customers in Britain cannot reach their money — the Guardian reports — after
the app failed on card payments, cash withdrawals and transfers.
The company calls it a service disruption and says funds and data are safe.
Sign up, sign in, cards, transfers, cash machines and crypto are all partly down.
Open the app and the message is something went wrong.
Try again later.
Revolute says it has been on the fault since this morning and has apologized.
The Guardian says the break may sit with Google Cloud, which Revolute uses under a partner
to run its systems.
Google reported elevated errors in intermittent network failures on multiple cloud services in
the Europe West 2 region and said it had no work around.
Other Fintech firms are hit as well.
All-Stom, the French train maker, has a first-trench order of about 800 million euros for
metropolis trains on Hanoi's urban rail, the Investor Reports.
The company said Monday the trains belong to an October 6 deal with Vin Group and will
be designed and built at Valenciennes Petite-Farre.
The order books in the third quarter of Allstom's 2026, 2027 year. Allstom will build up to 83 trains in France.
Vin Homes, the Vin Group subsidiary, will assemble up to 117 more in Vietnam from Allstom parts, under a technology license.
The sets are five cars, with new designs Allstom says are meant to raise efficiency and passenger safety.
Hanoi's 100-year master plan aims at 979 kilometers and 18 lines by 2045, as the backbone
of city transport, to cut congestion and pollution.
Allstom has been in Vietnam more than 30 years.
It modernized signaling and telecoms on both phases of the Hanoi to Vin Line and equipped
Ninh Binh station.
On Metro Line 3, it already supplied 10 4-car metropolis trains from France, plus Urbalis 400 signaling,
power gear and depot systems.
South Korea's foreign ministry will pull more embassy staff out of Ukraine, all Jazeera
reports, after what Seoul calls Kyiv's lack of a constructive reply on North Korean
prisoners of war.
spokesperson Park Do-soon said Tuesday that Seoul had used several channels and still had
no sufficient answer.
Earlier this month, the ambassador was recalled after President Vladimir Zelensky told the UN
General Assembly that Ukraine had handed two captured North Korean soldiers to the South.
South. Seoul says that transfer should have stayed secret to protect the soldier's families
in the North.
Asharje Defear stays in Kyiv, with every consular officer to look after South Korean nationals.
He also cited airstrike threats as a reason staff safety is hard to guarantee. Seoul had
already summoned Ukraine's ambassador and warned of further steps. Ukraine's line is
that diplomacy must prevail over emotions and that Kyiv considers the matter resolved.
Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said a message from Ukraine included words of apology, but fell
short of what Seoul wanted.
South Korea's constitution treats all North Koreans as citizens of the Republic of Korea,
and people who reach its territory and ask to defect are generally allowed to stay.
Alberta voters rejected a plan to hold an independence referendum, with about 76 percent against
an unofficial results all Jazeera carried, and more than 300,000 in favor.
The Guardian, using elections Alberta and more than 1.5 million votes, put the stay in
Canada share at 76% and the start a separation process share near 24.
Prime Minister Mark Carney, who grew up in Edmonton, said Albertans chose Unity and chose Canada.
Premier Danielle Smith said they voted for a stronger Alberta inside a United Canada.
Separatist Keith Wilson said at least a quarter feel the province needs better treatment.
The question was whether to stay or begin a legal path that could lead to a second vote,
one of 10 on the ballot, and elections Alberta said the rest of the count could take days.
About 100 of roughly 1,400 polling stations ran late, holding results more than two hours.
About 43% of eligible voters, 1.3 million people, had already voted early or by mail.
In Yemen, officials say Iranian-backed Houthi ballistic missiles killed dozens at a desert
military camp deep in government-held country and attack the New York Times called
among the deadliest of the renewed war. In Haiti, the mayor of Kenskhof wrote hundreds of
letters warning officials of gang threats near the Capitol than dozens of people died,
and so did he. Vietnam has signed a free trade deal with the four European free trade
association states after more than 14 years of talks, aiming at more trade, investment,
and cooperation. In Park City, Kansas, President Donald Trump said the agriculture department
will start an $8 billion diesel relief program in harvest season, so farmers can offset fuel costs.
France had a sign of progress overnight. France 24 says the first night of targeted
curfews passed without incident after weekend riots. And in Paris, Emerald Maxwell reported
no disturbance. Prime Minister Sebastian Lacornew said further curfews will be imposed on Tuesday
where they are necessary. That's OmniView top-world news for today. I'm Mira. See you tomorrow.
